watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, via cairn.machines.chart.verdict.write_verdict, carrying for each re-run: the verdict berth, the claim and instrument (the proof), the first run (exit, seconds, started, ended) and the alone run (exit, seconds), contention true or false, and the neighbours in flight during the first run (their claims and started/ended epochs). Plus the totals: re-runs, contention reds, re-run seconds against all run seconds of the same verdicts.
watchme.consumer: cc_0, which reviews the hypothesis at outline 9.4.8.1.1 against the pairs and rewrites it as we learn (outline 0.6.1).
watchme.enough: The numbers settle the hypothesis once >= 20 post-era re-runs are recorded. It HOLDS (CLEARED, outline 9.4.8.1.1 stands) when >= 4 of them turned green alone (the re-run catches real contention) and the re-runs' seconds are <= 10% of all run seconds in the same verdicts (it is worth the time). It is REWRITTEN to 'record the red as it came' when 0 of 20 turned green alone, or when the re-runs cost > 25% of those seconds. Any other split: cc_0 rewrites the hypothesis from the numbers and the watch runs on. If 30 days pass from PROVED with fewer than 20 re-runs, that scarcity is the reading: cc_0 reviews with what has come in.
watchme.trigger: Every verdict berthed after this ticket's PROVED crossing (the era floor) whose readings carry an alone re-run: the verdict's own berth write, the event that already fires. The probe reads ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/verdict-*.json newer than the PROVED crossing and takes every reading with a run_alone.
